Guidance & outlook: According to PwC's Global Entertainment & Media Outlook, the industry grew to reach US$3.5 trillion in revenues and is expected to grow by a further 4.6% in 2026, on its way to surpassing US$4.2 trillion by the turn of the decade.
The sector is now projected to reach INR 3.3 trillion by 2028, with digital media, live events, filmed entertainment and animation and VFX expected to be the primary engines of that growth.

Outlook FY 2025-26 marks a clear positive inflection in the Group's consolidated performance, with EBITDA up 52%, margins expanding across MA2, WWI and Bahrain, and the consolidated net loss narrowing by nearly a third.
Growth & demand: According to the FICCI- EY report released earlier this year, the sector grew by approximately 9% in 2025, comfortably outpacing nominal GDP growth and marking a decisive return to form after two years of more muted performance.

Digital media crossed the INR 1 trillion mark for the first time, cementing its position as the largest segment within our industry, while digital advertising grew by 26% and live events surged by an extraordinary 44%.

Because MA2's cost base is largely fixed, this revenue growth flowed through to the bottom line at a disproportionately favourable rate: while total expenses grew only 6% (IND-AS 116 adjusted), revenue grew 16% on the same basis, driving the EBITDA margin (IND-AS 116 adjusted) from -2% to a positive 7%.
Margins & costs: On a consolidated basis, Revenue from Operations grew while Consolidated EBITDA rose sharply with EBITDA margin expanding meaningfully to 15%.
174.2 million - a 52% increase - with EBITDA margin expanding from 10% to 15%.

160.8 million, and as a result the Company preserved a robust EBITDA margin of 49% (FY25: 50%) - a testament to the efficiency of the standalone cost base even in a year without a new content release.
Capex & expansion: The increase in employee benefit costs (14%) reflects deliberate investment in institutional quality - a 6.5% annual increment cycle and the conversion of consulting faculty to staff roles - while higher other expenses reflect WWI's expanding brand visibility, including its YouTube facility and hosting the IC3 conference at BKC.

Upon completion, the investment in Mukta A2, where the Company presently holds 70% of shareholding will reduce between 49% to 42% (i.e. post conversion of Compulsorily Convertible Debentures) of shareholding and Mukta A2 will transit from being a subsidiary to an associate of the Company.

At the same time, industry data shows this growth was substantially price-led - average ticket prices rose approximately 20% even as overall admissions declined, underscoring that footfall recovery, rather than pricing alone, remains the industry's central long-term challenge.
